newsitem.title: USA: CNS says made aware of similar product.
newsitem.headline: CNS says made aware of similar product.

text.p: CNS Inc, which makes a Breathe Right strip used to treat nasal congestion, said Thursday it has become aware of a foreign reference to a nasal dilator, not commercially available, and plans to discuss the implications with the U.S. Patent and Trademark office.
CNS said it will continue to own exclusive and enforceable patent protection for the Breathe Right strip.
The company also said two configurations of the Breathe Right strip will be introduced in the fall.

One is a nearly transparent version of the strips, and the other is a kit to be marketed by Perrigo Co, a large private-label drug manufacturer. The kit will combine Breathe Right nasal strips with store-brand nasal sprays.

Advertising for the strip during the summer months will remain relatively light and will include a joint promotion with Universal Pictures scheduled for August to coincide with the release of the movie "Leave It to Beaver." CNS said it expects to increase its advertising with a new, stronger campaign in the fall as the cold season begins.

Earlier, CNS reported 1997 second quarter sales fell to $13.6 million from $21.1 million in the second quarter last year. The company's U.S. sales of $12.6 million were equal to U.S. sales reported in the second quarter last year. International sales of $1.0 million were sharply below the sales of $8.5 million reported in last year's second quarter, when there were large shipments to begin filling the international distribution pipeline.
Net income fell to $2.61 million or $0.13 a share from $3.05 million or $0.15 a year ago.

CNS designs, makes and markets consumer products, including a Breathe Right nasal strip, which it says improves breathing by reducing nasal airflow resistance. It is used to eliminate or reduce snoring, and to temporarily relieve nasal congestion.
